references.text: The same theme of rejoicing before the Lord for all the good He has given, together with one's entire household.
A command to rejoice before the Lord along with sons, daughters, servants, and the Levite, paralleling the inclusion of the Levite in the joy.
Rejoicing before the Lord with the whole household and the Levite is mentioned again as a repeated command.
At the Feast of Tabernacles, one shall rejoice together with the Levite and the foreigner, the same groups mentioned here.
A command to rejoice at the festival together with the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
The instruction to love the foreigner who lives among you, related to the care for the foreigner in this verse.
The Levite and the foreigner shall come and eat and be satisfied, showing care for these same groups.
The continuation of the text dealing with the tithe for the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
